clue.text: The frozen lea?

parts.note: a lea is a meadow, so a meadow turned solid by frost suggests a vast expanse of polar ice

explanation.surface: A wintry meadow, white with frost.
explanation.walkthrough: Lea is a poetic word for a field or meadow; freeze it solid and you have a great sheet of ice.
explanation.definitionFit: An expanse of permanent ice, as in polar regions, is pictured as a meadow made of ice.

clue.text: Firm with good man taking only second half that is valuable

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
ST, short for saint, is the crossword's usual good man

indicators.note: the second half of the word only is its last two letters

explanation.surface: A company adopts a saintly figure, keeping only part of him, and that proves worthwhile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second half' takes LY from 'only'. 'taking' and 'that is' just join the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something valuable costs a lot of money, so it is expensive.

clue.text: Old French settler

parts.note: reads like one of the Franks who settled Gaul, but means a former French coin that settled a bill

explanation.surface: An early colonist in the land that became France.
explanation.walkthrough: The Franks settled Gaul and gave France its name, so the solver thinks of a tribesman; the settler is in fact money, which settles debts. France's currency before the euro was the franc.
explanation.definitionFit: The former French currency unit paid, and so settled, accounts before the euro replaced it.

clue.text: Neat prose translated into another language

indicators.note: translated suggests words recast into a new form, so the letters of neat prose are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tidy writing rendered into a foreign tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' fits the language theme of the surface but here signals rearranging the letters of NEAT PROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is an artificial international language devised by Zamenhof in 1887.

clue.text: Mother country within 24 hours an old African country

indicators.note: within says the mother country piece sits inside the word for 24 hours

parts.note: a day lasts 24 hours
one's mother country is one's home

explanation.surface: Somebody visits the land of their birth for a single day, then an African nation is named.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' puts HOME inside DAY, between its A and Y; 'an' only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dahomey was the West African state renamed Benin in 1975.

clue.text: Not straightforward, not about to accuse

indicators.note: the second not tells us to leave out the word for about from the longer word

parts.note: something not straightforward is indirect
RE is Latin-derived for about, as in a business letter

explanation.surface: Someone is evasive and yet stops short of making a charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'not' removes RE from INDIRECT, leaving INDICT.
explanation.definitionFit: To indict is to charge formally with a crime.

clue.text: Inspire one doctor with acceptable energy

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
U means upper-class and so socially acceptable, in British usage
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: One physician, fair and full of vigour, motivates others.
explanation.walkthrough: U as 'acceptable' comes from the old British U and non-U division of upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbue someone is to fill them with a feeling or quality, much as to inspire them does.

clue.text: Main meal prepared and served on this?

parts.note: dinner is the main meal of the day
set means ready, prepared

explanation.surface: The principal meal is ready and dished up.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a question: a whole matching collection of plates is what the main meal is served on.
explanation.definitionFit: A matching collection of plates and dishes is what food is put on at table.

clue.text: Vehicle taking cotton thread from the city

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
lisle is a fine, strong cotton thread used for stockings

explanation.surface: A car loads up cotton thread brought out of town.
explanation.walkthrough: Carlisle is a city in Cumbria, northwest England, near the Scottish border.
explanation.definitionFit: Carlisle is an English cathedral town in Cumbria, so it is an example of a city.

clue.text: Cares about leading penny onto slope

indicators.note: leading says the jumbled piece goes in front of the coin letter
about here means moved around, so the letters of cares are mixed up

explanation.surface: Concerns about a coin rolling down a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges CARES into ESCAR, which 'leading' puts ahead of P.
explanation.definitionFit: An escarp is a steep bank or incline, the same as an escarpment.

clue.text: Husband Jack had time to include one Cuban dance

indicators.note: to include says the run of pieces wraps round the word for one

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, and AB, able seaman, is a sailor
an era is a period of time
an means one, as in an apple

explanation.surface: A married sailor had enough time to take one more turn on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: H and AB 'had' ERA, giving HABERA, and 'to include' puts AN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The habanera is a slow dance in duple time that originated in Havana.

clue.text: Used to pluck a guitar

parts.note: describes the small flat tool a player holds to strike the strings

explanation.surface: A guitarist's accessory.
explanation.definitionFit: A pick, a thin piece of plastic or horn, strikes the strings of a stringed instrument.

clue.text: Naturally it is cover for the pupil

definitions.text: Naturally it is cover for the pupil

parts.words: Naturally it is cover for the pupil
parts.note: pupil reads as a schoolchild needing a substitute teacher, but means the dark centre of the eye, shielded by a fold of skin

explanation.surface: Of course a supply teacher steps in for the schoolchild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover' and 'pupil' suggest school: a stand-in teacher covering a class. The pupil is the eye's, and its natural cover is the lid.
explanation.definitionFit: The fold of skin that closes over the eye shields it from light and dust.

clue.text: Least expensive music-maker?

parts.note: the cheapest instrument would cost a coin of the lowest value, and the question mark flags the play

explanation.surface: The cheapest instrument money can buy.
explanation.walkthrough: The tin whistle is called by the name of the smallest British coin because it cost almost nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheap tin flute with six holes is named after the smallest coin, which is what it once cost.

clue.text: Ample input fell dramatically

indicators.note: dramatically suggests a sudden upheaval, so the letters of input fell are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: The contribution plunged sharply, though there was plenty of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dramatically' rearranges INPUT FELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample and plentiful are synonyms: more than enough.

clue.text: Lash stallion perhaps and move rapidly

parts.note: a stallion is an example of a horse, so perhaps flags the example
to whip is to move quickly, as in whip round the corner

explanation.surface: Strike the stallion and make it gallop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lash' is the verb, to flog, matching the verb formed by the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog someone with a riding crop is to thrash them, as to lash does.

clue.text: It is used for grilling on the playing-field

definitions.meaning: a metal grate of parallel bars over a fire for cooking meat
the American football pitch, marked with parallel lines

explanation.surface: A cooking grate is taken out to the sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The American football field is nicknamed for its parallel yard lines, which resemble a cooking grate.
explanation.definitionFit: A barred grate for cooking meat, and by its striped look the pitch for American football.

clue.text: Honour showing relative success in exam results

definitions.meaning: a British award limited to 24 members, founded by Edward VII
a ranking of candidates from best to worst

explanation.surface: An award for the student who tops the results table.
explanation.walkthrough: The British award limited to 24 holders, and a list ranking candidates by how well they did.
explanation.definitionFit: A British distinction given by the sovereign, and a ranking of candidates by how well they performed.

clue.text: Mother smeared cream on ornamental string work

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: smeared means spread messily, so the letters of cream are rearranged

explanation.surface: Mum spread cream over a decorative knotted wall-hanging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smeared' rearranges CREAM into CRAME, set after MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Macramé is decorative craftwork of knotted cord, a kind of knotted lace.

clue.text: A few arranged loan on island

parts.note: the wordplay needs V, the Roman numeral five

indicators.note: arranged means set in a new order, so the letters of loan are shuffled

explanation.surface: A small number set up a loan on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed 'few' cannot give V; read 'five', the Roman numeral V. 'arranged' rearranges LOAN into ALON.
explanation.definitionFit: Avalon is the legendary isle where King Arthur was carried after his last battle.

clue.text: Short poem from a lady!

definitions.meaning: playfully, a little ode, with the French diminutive ending added
a woman's given name, borne by the swan princess in Swan Lake

explanation.surface: A brief verse written by a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a joke: add the French diminutive ending -ette to a lyric poem and you have a short one. The exclamation mark flags the fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A coined diminutive of a lyric poem, and a French woman's given name.

clue.text: Regretted capturing flighty creature

indicators.note: capturing says the bird is held inside the word regretted

explanation.surface: Someone was sorry they had trapped a skittish animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flighty' looks like nervous but means able to fly: the creature is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The egret, a white heron, is a bird, and birds take flight.

clue.text: Make about four new and original

indicators.note: about says the word for make goes round the numeral four

parts.note: to create is to make
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Produce roughly four fresh and inventive works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts IV inside CREATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Inventive work shows imagination and novelty, being fresh rather than copied.

clue.text: Shakespearean book

parts.note: points to the title character of one of the Bard's plays set in Athens

explanation.surface: A volume by the Bard.
explanation.walkthrough: Timon of Athens is one of Shakespeare's plays; its title character, a rich man turned misanthrope, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The misanthrope of Athens is the title figure of one of the Bard's lesser-known plays.

clue.text: Invoice for latter one is said to follow

indicators.note: to follow puts the sounded piece after the word for for

parts.note: pro means for, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: is said means the piece is heard spoken, not written

parts.note: in the pairing former and latter, the partner word that comes before the latter one

explanation.surface: A bill for the second item, which we are told will come later.
explanation.walkthrough: In 'the former ... the latter' pairing, the latter one goes with FORMER; spoken, that sounds like FORMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A provisional bill sent in advance of goods, as a pro forma, is a kind of invoice.

clue.text: Bee of low birth!

parts.note: an old name for the bumblebee joins a word meaning lowly to the insect

explanation.surface: An insect of lowly origins.
explanation.walkthrough: The bumblebee was once called the humble-bee, and the word left over also means of lowly origin.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means of low social rank, and is also the first part of an old name for the bumblebee.

clue.text: From Kathleen he removed jewellery

indicators.note: removed means taken out and also moved about, so take the letters of he from Kathleen and rearrange the rest

explanation.surface: Kathleen's husband took away her trinkets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' takes H and E out of KATHLEEN; the remaining KATLEN rearranges to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental band worn round the ankle is a kind of jewellery.

clue.text: Interpreter was quiet with single book

parts.note: ex means formerly, something that was
P, piano, means quiet in music
one means single
NT, the New Testament, is a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A translator once kept silent with just one volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was' gives EX, as in ex-wife, someone who was one.
explanation.definitionFit: An exponent is one who sets forth or explains something, such as a performer interpreting music.
